s1.syndrome_frame: Acute vision loss with intraocular hemorrhage and crystalline deposits
salient_findings: Glistening crystals in the anterior chamber
Iridescent, needle-like crystals in the aqueous
key_facts: The patient is a young girl
The right eye is blind
Hyphema developed spontaneously
Vitreous hemorrhage occurred
Multiple glistening crystals were observed in the anterior chamber
The number of aqueous crystals increased as the hyphema resolved
Iridescent, needle-like crystals were seen floating in the aqueous
A morning glory optic disc anomaly was present
There was a low-lying detachment of the peripapillary retina
Chronic retinal detachment was visualized after vitreous hemorrhage resolution

differentials: Acute posterior multifocal placoid pigment epitheliopathy
per_call: Acute posterior multifocal placoid pigment epitheliopathy

shortlist.label: Bietti crystalline corneoretinal dystrophy
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of iridescent, needle-like crystals in the aqueous humor

shortlist.label: Primary hyperoxaluria
shortlist.why_kept: Spontaneous hyphema and vitreous hemorrhage with crystalline deposits

shortlist.label: Cystinosis
shortlist.why_kept: Crystalline deposits in the eye, consistent with cystine accumulation

shortlist.label: Morning glory syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Morning glory optic disc anomaly and low-lying detachment of the peripapillary retina

shortlist.label: Sjögren-Larsson syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Crystalline deposits and retinal detachment, although less common in this condition

raw.rationale: The presence of a morning glory optic disc anomaly, low-lying detachment of the peripapillary retina, and chronic retinal detachment are key features that align with Morning glory syndrome, which is known to cause such ocular abnormalities.

rejected.label: Bietti crystalline corneoretinal dystrophy
rejected.why: While it involves crystals in the eye, it primarily affects the cornea and retina, not typically associated with morning glory disc anomaly or the specific retinal detachments described.

rejected.label: Primary hyperoxaluria
rejected.why: This condition involves oxalate crystals but is more commonly associated with kidney stones and systemic issues rather than the specific ocular findings described.

rejected.label: Cystinosis
rejected.why: Cystinosis can cause crystals in the eye, but it is a systemic disease with significant renal and other systemic manifestations not mentioned in the vignette.

rejected.label: Sjögren-Larsson syndrome
rejected.why: This condition involves retinal changes but is primarily known for ichthyosis and neurologic symptoms, which are not described in the case.
